title: 3D Force-Directed Network Graph (Social Network Visualization)
prompt:
Create a "3D force-directed graph" social network visualization using Three.js.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
The following importmap must be included in the HTML <head> exactly as written, and imports must use ES Modules inside <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
// Write your code here
</script>

[Graph Data]
(1) Hard-code a social network in the code with exactly 50 nodes and 80 undirected edges.
(2) Each node must contain: name (string) and group (an integer from 0–4, for a total of 5 groups). Each edge must contain source and target (node indices or ids).

[Force-Directed Simulation]
(3) Implement a force-directed simulation that updates every frame (do not use an existing graph library as a black box to encapsulate the entire simulation, but classic formulas may be referenced):
    - Coulomb repulsion between nodes (all-pairs repulsion)
    - Spring attraction along edges (the natural length may be the geometric distance when the edge is created or a fixed restLength)
    - Weak attraction toward the origin/centering to prevent the entire graph from dispersing
(4) Use semi-implicit Euler integration or a similar numerical integration method, with a reasonably small dt; the position and velocity of each pinned node must remain fixed, with its velocity set to 0 (it must not move).

[Rendering]
(5) Nodes must be spheres (THREE.Mesh), with 5 distinguishable colors used for the 5 groups.
(6) Node radius (or scale) must be monotonically related to degree (more connections means a larger node).
(7) Edges must use THREE.Line or LineSegments, and their vertex positions must update with the nodes every frame.
(8) Use OrbitControls to view the scene.

[Interaction]
(9) Hovering the mouse over a node: highlight that node and its neighbors (any clear visual distinction is sufficient), and display the node's name in id="hoverInfo".
(10) Clicking a node: toggle that node between pin and unpin; pinned nodes must not move during the simulation.
(11) id="pauseBtn": a button that toggles between pause and resume; while paused, integration updates must stop while preserving the current layout.

[HUD]
(12) id="nodeCount": the number of nodes (must be 50).
(13) id="edgeCount": the number of edges (must be 80).
(14) id="simEnergy": display a scalar simulation "energy/temperature" value (for example, total kinetic energy plus a simplified sum of potential energy related to equilibrium positions, or the sum of squared velocities; it must be finite and able to change while the simulation is running).
(15) id="pinnedCount": the current number of pinned nodes.

[State Exposure (Required)]
Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame, including at least:
- nodeCount: number
- edgeCount: number
- nodes: Array<{ x, y, z, name, group, pinned, degree }>
- simEnergy: number
- isPaused: boolean
- pinnedCount: number

Output a single HTML file that can be opened directly in a browser. All coordinates and energy values must be finite; NaN/Infinity must never occur.
physics_constraints: Coulomb repulsion + spring attraction along edges + centering force
Pinned nodes: zero velocity, fixed position during simulation steps
simEnergy finite whenever simulation state is queried
